beats.narration_en: Why is the end of this runway built to crumble?
Sometimes a jet can't stop and runs off the end.
So many airports add a bed of crushable concrete blocks.
It looks like pavement, but it's light and full of bubbles.
Under the weight of a plane, the blocks crush.
The tires sink in, like driving into deep sand.
Every block they crush takes away some of the speed.
It's built to stop a jet rolling in at eighty miles an hour.
It has already stopped more than two dozen planes, with hundreds aboard.
Afterward, crews just replace the crushed blocks.
That's the gray pad at the end of some runways.
